Date: 2026-09-07T08:12:00Z
Subject: VM artefacts request + regression eval clarification

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement SIG review and our internal SOC 2 evidence pack, Helix needs the following from Redwood: a concise scan ledger (last 90 days), a mapping of active CVE ownership for high/critical items, and any regression evaluation artifacts you use to verify that remediation doesn't cause functional regressions (sample tests, results, or links).

Can you also confirm your SLA for CVE remediation SLAs for critical vs high severities (we expect target windows and any escalation path) and whether you have an escrow or hotfix policy for production hotpatching? Our deadline for the vendor pack is 2026-09-15.

If it's helpful I can accept a single zipped bundle or a Drive folder link.

Regards,
Elaine Su
Senior Security Engineer
Helix Financial

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-09-07T12:34:00Z
Subject: Re: VM artefacts request + regression eval clarification

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the clear ask. We've bundled the requested artifacts and included a short readme to explain each item. Contents: 
- redwood-scan-ledger-202608.zip: aggregate scan results (last 90 days) with anonymized host IDs and vulnerability severity mapping.
- cve-ownership-matrix.xlsx: who owns remediation, expected target window, and current status.
- patch-plan-202609.pdf: sample hotfix process and rollback playbook used for high/critical remediation.
- regression-eval-samples/: smoke & integration test snapshots we run after patching.

Quick answers: our standard SLA targets are: critical: 7 days to remediation plan & emergency patch cadence; high: 30 days to remediation plan, 90 days to closure for most high items unless exploitability elevates priority. For customers with Dedicated or Private plans we offer tighter SLAs under contract — we can call out contract-specific terms in your pack if that matters.

I also want to highlight our regression evaluation: we run a two-phase pipeline — (1) smoke/regression acceptance tests against a staging model serving cluster within 24 hours of patch validation, and (2) a short production verification window (synthetic traffic + canary rollout) before full rollout. Evidence samples are in the bundle.

I've attached the bundle and included a short attestation letter. If you need a signed attestation, let me know and I can route to Legal.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales (Security Programs)
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa —

Quick status:
- CVE-2026-1845 (model-runtime lib): assigned to infra-team/model-runtime (owner: ekaterina@redwoodinference.com). Remediation plan: backport + rebuild kernel; ETA for patch artifact: 2026-09-10. Canary deploy targeted 2026-09-11.
- CVE-2026-3032 (third-party dependency): triage complete; mitigation via pinned dependency + container patch. ETA for remediation plan: 2026-09-14; closure 2026-10-02.
- CVE-2025-9987 (low-exploitability high sev): mitigation scheduled; closure expected 2026-09-28.

Regression validation: testing snapshots are in the regression-eval-samples directory. We run a 3-stage validation: unit -> integrated smoke -> synthetic workload canary. We will redact any customer PII before sending the snapshots to Helix.

I'll assemble a short attestation paragraph we can include in the bundle: describe scan cadence (weekly internal scans, monthly external auth scans), SLA windows, and a confirmatory line about rollback capability and canary policy.

- CVE SLA targets: Critical: emergency plan within 7 days + expedited hotfix cadence; High: remediation plan within 30 days and closure typically within 90 days unless escalated. We have contractual tighter SLAs for Dedicated customers.
- Regression verification: smoke/integration tests + canary window; we maintain rollback playbooks and automated verification to minimize risk of regression.
